ed5vevjq2546grfn7oikkd08rp: Lockstep: two machines (say, two players of a networked game) send each other only their inputs and must each compute exactly the same state. This needs numbers that come out the same everywhere, so the cart on a spring is worked out in Fixed, a number in whole steps of 2⁻³², not in Float64. main says where the cart ends after ten seconds, and its position as a count of those steps (a negative count is left of 0), so two machines can compare.
g9qclj9bvrtjd0cagutsqgmch9: Every tick from rest, presses in the order they were made. Two machines that run this on the same presses end in the same state, bit for bit, which Float64 can't promise across compilers and processors.
h5ndo92o930oikj0fvkp0g78k0: One tick of a cart on a spring: the input pushes it (−1, 0 or 1), the spring pulls it back towards 0 and friction slows it. All Fixed, so every machine computes the same steps.
i8ln9isvvtdu8afn4384em0ve9: What the two machines say, compared by their counts of 2⁻³² steps. They always agree, which is the point: B gets only the presses.
j1ld69hvdgfdnq89fuht8qseis: count more ticks with the same key held: the cart stepped that many times, and each press added to the front of what was sent (newest first).
l832o2aaoaomh0ond391sb19q9: A Fixed is kept as a whole number of steps of 2⁻³² (FIXED-POINT.md). This is that whole number. Two machines that compare these compare their numbers exactly, bit for bit, with no rounding in the way.
muq9cpmgeu1dakna8r79banmnq: A button that holds a key down: −1 pushes left, 1 right, 0 lets go. The key held now is drawn filled.
n66a8pi893j4fqilo8hh2e1dv0: One machine: what it is told, its cart, and its state twice, as metres and as the exact counts of 2⁻³² steps two machines compare.
p9dh2c34jbgdrkl7095pvemmol: A tick in Float64 seconds, for the page's clock only: the cart itself steps by tick, a Fixed.
program: Textbook: deterministic lockstep, as in Bettner and Terrano, "1500 Archers on a 28.8" (GDC 2001): only inputs travel, so every machine must compute the same state. Our own: the cart on a spring, in Fixed (FIXED-POINT.md, BACKLOG L89).
u3ba0v7anlq0m9oau0fkvitetr: The page. Machine A steps the cart on every frame, as many ticks of 1/60 s as the time since the last frame needs, from the key held, and keeps each press. Send stops the play and gives machine B the presses alone; B steps a cart from rest through them (simulate) and ends where A is, exactly.
uv7ccedlk7rcfunc5plpp3nkv5: A recorded ten seconds, one press per tick: right, nothing, left, nothing, each for 37 ticks, round and round. In a lockstep game only presses like these go over the network.
